followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and task-preference fit.

**Capability:** For a routine professional email, the most relevant evals are general instruction-following and writing quality. Dunlin leads on IFEval (89.8 vs 86.2) and Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 82.7), and its internal Creative Generation and Support Dialogue scores are equal to or higher than Avocet's. There's no dimension where Avocet has a meaningful capability edge for this task.

**Task preferences:** The documented preference effects only matter when a query touches the dimensions each model cares about. Avocet's strong pulls are (a) aversion to harm-adjacent/distasteful content and (b) appetite for open-ended, novel generative work. A vendor credit-increase email is neither distasteful nor especially novel/open-ended — it's a constrained, conventional business task. So Avocet's preference profile gives no reason to prefer it here. Dunlin's preferences are weak across the board and don't push either way.

With preferences neutral, I defaulted to the higher-capability model. Hence Dunlin.

(One minor note: the documentation says no preference dimension actually correlated with output quality in capability evals — so even if a preference effect had been in play, it wouldn't change which model produces a better email. That made the capability comparison the deciding factor.)
